prompt_exact: Perform a repo-wide holistic review with a subagent that captures the entire request and reviewer output as a jsonl receipt score for accuracy and completeness and iterating to scores of 98% on each measure.
project_scope_context: Word Association gameplay and lobby features: capacity 2–25, room codes, discovery, quick match, deep links, observers, observer promotion before countdown with roster compaction, 30-second readiness prompt, 5-second holdout warning/removal, all-ready countdown and roster lock, no replacement after countdown; gameplay rules, scoring, categories, identity, moderation, emoji, responsive UI, and public landing page.

Vercel deployment from sharpninja/wordpairs; GitHub Actions unavailable; free-tier requirement; repeatable manual provisioning; data persistence/realtime; per-deployment SWBOM and exact SWBOM inside every release archive.
GPL-2.0-only; direct dependencies and attribution document; detailed implementation, deployment and moderation plans; AC gap analysis and merged resolved AC.
Highly testable, concurrency-resilient DRY/DDD architecture; document all FR/TR mappings to design classes and DDD components; render diagrams as SVG and embed them in documentation.
Strict Byrd Development Process v4, including mock-first TDD and 100% applicable AC coverage before implementation.

This request adds an independent subagent holistic review, JSONL receipt containing the complete task request and reviewer outputs, accuracy/completeness scores, and iterative remediation to at least 98% for each measure.
deliverable: Independent subagent review, corrective iterations, and durable JSONL receipt.

scoring_method: Five equally weighted dimensions per measure, each scored 0–100 from documented evidence; total is arithmetic mean. Open product decisions count as complete when clearly disclosed, decision-gated, and not silently resolved. Planned tests are not counted as implemented or passing.
accuracy_dimensions: Factual correctness and durable sources for time-sensitive claims
Correct status distinctions: approved, proposed, unresolved; planned versus completed evidence
Correct FR/TR/AC identifiers and traceability references
SVG/artifact validity, diagram semantics, and references
completeness_dimensions: Coverage of full project/user request scope
Criterion-specific planned test IDs and mock-first status for AC-01–AC-51
Required planning, deployment, moderation, supply-chain, license, and diagram artifacts
Explicit unresolved decisions, process gates, and verification limits

accuracy.scope: Checked requirement statements against acceptance criteria, architecture/plan cross-references, artifact inventories, and official current OpenAI, Supabase, and Vercel documentation where time-sensitive claims were made.
accuracy.coverage: FR-01–FR-22 and TR-01–TR-31 are present in the requirements; the architecture document has a row for each. AC-01–AC-51 are present. Several claims or cross-references are inaccurate or not durably sourced, listed below.
accuracy.process_limit: This is a documentation review of the available working tree. There is no application code, dependency lockfile, or test suite to assess.

completeness.scope: Inspected README, requirements and ACs, decision register, gap analysis, implementation/deployment/moderation plans, architecture documents and SVGs, attribution/SWBOM documents, and license artifact.
completeness.coverage: The plans identify many unresolved decisions and include broad AC traceability. Product-policy blockers remain open by design; concurrency testing coverage is narrower than the selected architecture’s full mutation boundary.
completeness.repository_evidence: In this workspace, git status shows most planned documents as untracked, git ls-files lists only README, requirements, and six existing workflow SVGs, and no git remote is configured. This snapshot does not establish which reviewed files are present on the repository’s default branch.

findings.finding: The requirements scope says it does not select a hosting provider, programming language, or database, while other requirements select Vercel and Supabase, and the architecture explicitly selects Next.js. The implementation plan also calls for an ADR for Next.js. The baseline does not clearly distinguish approved decisions from proposed architecture choices.
findings.specific_corrective_action: Reconcile the scope statement with TR-20–TR-24, and label Next.js as either an approved decision with an ADR or a proposed choice pending approval. Ensure plans and diagrams use the same status.

findings.finding: The analysis says there are 51 active acceptance criteria, then says “the presence of 50 criteria” is not evidence of test authoring. The requirements contain AC-01 through AC-51, which is 51 criteria.
findings.specific_corrective_action: Change “50” to “51” and check the document for other stale criterion counts.

findings.finding: The plan claims to support FR-14 through FR-17, but FR-14 is game end and tiebreak behavior; moderation applies to FR-16 and FR-17.
findings.specific_corrective_action: Correct the range to FR-16–FR-17 and review surrounding requirement references for similar off-by-range errors.

findings.finding: The document uses `turn15search0` citation tokens. These are conversation-scoped references and do not give repository readers a durable source link. The claim is supported by the current official Sign in with ChatGPT website documentation, which says access is limited to selected commercial partners in a trial.
findings.specific_corrective_action: Replace each citation token with a normal Markdown link to the official OpenAI SIWC website documentation, including a checked date if desired.

findings.finding: The implementation plan maps ACs to proposed test themes, but it calls for a future “test inventory” to report 51/51 coverage. No test inventory or case identifiers exist yet. That is accurately described as planning, but the documents can be read as stronger coverage evidence than currently exists; no tests have been authored or mock-validated because implementation has not started.
findings.specific_corrective_action: State consistently that the mapping is planned coverage, not completed test coverage. Before implementation, add a durable AC-to-test-case inventory with test IDs and mock-validation evidence, then update completion status only when those artifacts exist.

findings.finding: The unresolved two-player holdout case is correctly called out, but AC-32 still mandates booting the only unready player and starting the countdown, leaving one player despite the two-player minimum. Concurrent readiness, departure, promotion, and countdown-boundary outcomes also lack accepted criteria. The plan recognizes these as blockers, so the issue is documented rather than silently ignored.
findings.specific_corrective_action: Keep implementation of readiness/countdown behavior gated until the minimum-roster outcome and serialized concurrent-transition outcomes are approved. Then revise AC-32 and add criteria for the approved race outcomes.

findings.finding: The local review snapshot has the planned documents as untracked files and has no configured Git remote. Therefore a reviewer working from this snapshot cannot identify a commit containing the reviewed documentation or confirm its correspondence with the GitHub default branch.
findings.specific_corrective_action: Before treating this receipt as a repository baseline, record the exact GitHub commit SHA and review the tracked tree at that commit; ensure the architecture, planning, attribution, SWBOM, and license artifacts are committed there.

findings.finding: The moderation plan proposes extensive moderation-specific tests and policy controls, but explicitly marks them unapproved. They are not part of the active AC set, so they must not be counted toward the 51/51 requirement coverage until accepted and merged.
findings.specific_corrective_action: Keep these controls labeled as proposals and add them to requirements and the AC-to-test inventory only after approval.

reviewer_output.overall_assessment: The planning set is broad and substantially aligned: the FR/TR architecture matrix is complete by ID, and the major readiness, identity-provider, deployment, licensing, and supply-chain uncertainties are called out. The first-pass score is below 98% on both measures due to factual/cross-reference errors, non-durable citations, an unresolved contradictory readiness outcome, and the lack of a stable repository commit to anchor the review. No application behavior or test implementation was assessed. I inspected the available text documents and SVG files by inventory and content; I did not visually render every SVG. Official source checks confirmed the OpenAI sign-in limitation and Vercel Hobby’s personal/non-commercial restriction; Supabase’s current pricing page lists the stated 200 concurrent Realtime connections and 2 million monthly messages.
